newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end lower on weak futures, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end lower on weak futures, profit-taking.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower on Thursday, with late afternoon profit-taking wiping out the morning's fragile gains, brokers said.
"The market was led down partly by futures trading and partly by profit-taking," said Peter Lui, institutional sales manager at NAVA SC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed 81.15 points lower at 12,055.17, after swinging widely, hitting an opening low of 12,031.51, then clambering to a midday high of 12,270.66 before tumbling again.
Turnover was a respectable HK$6.98 billion, though down from Wednesday's HK$7.06 billion.
"Volume was relatively low in the morning, so it was easy to push the market up and down," said one broker. "I think we are going to continue to see more volatility in the market."
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was active with a total of 20,811 April contracts traded. The contract closed 25 points lower at 12,010 after hitting a late morning high of 12,255.
Brokers said there was some buying interest in second and third line issues by retail investors, and that institutions were largely sidelined.
Property and property-related stocks led the market down in late afternoon.
Cheung Kong lost HK$0.75 to HK$63.50, while subsidiary Hutchison Whampoa tumbled HK$1.75 to HK$54.00.
Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$0.75 to HK$77.00.
Banking giant HSBS Holdings lost HK$2.00 to HK$175.50, while Hang Seng Bank added HK$1.00 to HK78.75.
"On a fundamental basis, HSBC is now trading on a PE (price earnings ratio) of 10.5 times 1997 earnings, said Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Red chips came under profit-taking pressure with the notable exception of CITIC Pacific. The share was unchanged at HK$37.50.
China Resources slipped HK$0.20 to HK$16.25 on trade of HK$25.71 million. China Resources Beijing Land was also unchanged at HK$4.675. Shanghai Industrial shed HK$0.50 to HK$34.00.
Red chip property company Shum Yip Investment bucked the trend, adding HK$0.05 to HK$3.925.
H share Guangdong Kelon lost HK$0.15 to HK$6.60.
